article.title: Hegseth’s impeachment dodge, the draft, & the troops who won’t fight | w/ Mike Prysner
article.author: Zoe Alexandra
article.content: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth dodged impeachment this week thanks to 11 no-show Democrats on Hakeem Jeffries’ watch. Mike Prysner, Iraq War veteran and executive director of the Center on Conscience and War, joins Zoe Alexandra and Rania Khalek to unpack the charges in Rep. Thomas Massie’s articles of impeachment – from an illegal war on Iran that opened with the bombing of the Minab girls’ school, to a boat strike killing spree in the Caribbean and Pacific that has left more than 230 people dead. Opposition to war got Democrats elected, Prysner says, and at the first chance to deliver, “they just completely slept on it.” Prysner says conscientious objector filings are at a 25-year high, and they nearly all cite Minab. Not afraid for their own lives, he says; they refuse to hurt people they have no reason to hurt. He explains why a generation that grew up watching Gaza on their phones won’t fight in Trump’s wars, and why Hegseth’s Christian nationalist, anti-DEI overhaul of the military targeting women and Black soldiers is driving even more troops out. So starting next month, eligible young men will be automatically registered for the military draft. Prysner explains what automatic Selective Service registration really means – and how to prepare. Watch full episodes of BT Live, join breakthroughnews.org as a member today! #breakthroughnews ****** Rough transcript follows: [Speaker 1:] What is set to change on December 18th is that you will no longer have the choice to not register. You will be registered for the draft automatically by Grock or Palantir or whatever AI company. They’re going to scrape the data of Americans and put them on this draft list. It has a lot of problems. It puts you on a draft list when you don’t want to be, making you eligible to be drafted. Even being on the list should be a problem because the draft system was created as a show of force for the US to intimidate and threaten countries around the world. It was created during the Soviet intervention in Afghanistan, where the US was supporting Osama bin Laden. It was specifically a show of force in the Cold War. This week, the US House of Representatives failed to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, thanks to 11 Democrats who skipped the vote. This impeachment motion was brought forward by Republican Representative Thomas Massie from Kentucky. He raised charges around Hegseth’s conduct regarding the war on Iran and the deadly strikes on alleged drug boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific. This failure to impeach Hegseth has opened up a broader conversation about Democrats’ ability to carry forward these promises and what Hegseth has done as Secretary of War, what it has meant for the US military, and his attempts to deify the US military. To talk about these aspects and what it means, we are joined by Mike Prysner, a US Army veteran and the executive director of the Center on Conscience and War. Mike, thank you for joining us here at BT Live. [Speaker 2:] Thanks for having me. Again, on Tuesday, thank you to those 11 Democrats who, for some reason, just couldn’t be present for that vote. Great job, Hakeem Jeffries, just doing his job. It was the outgoing Republican Representative, Thomas Massie, who raised this impeachment of Pete Hegseth for his conduct in the Iran war and these boat strikes. Beyond this failure of the Democrats to carry this out, talk to us about these crimes. Why are the Pentagon’s actions in Iran and in the Caribbean and Pacific illegal? What are we talking about here? [Speaker 1:] It’s a violation of the War Powers Act, which has been going on for more than 60 days without congressional approval. Every administration in my lifetime has done this, especially in the war on terror era. It’s not abnormal, but the fact they are targeting Hegseth over this is significant. One of the main issues is the Minab school bombing, which has had resonance throughout the country and within the military. Of the more than 150 service members since the Iran war began who have filed as conscientious objectors, almost all mentioned the Minab school bombing as significant in their decision. For the administration, they want it to be something they gloss over, but it hasn’t gone away. We still receive calls from people for whom that was a turning point, leading them to take action to get out of the military. That being part of the articles of impeachment for Hegseth is important. His response to that was to hold a press conference saying he was proud of everything that happened and would do it again. The Pentagon’s investigation of the Minab school bombing claimed it was based on old intelligence, saying it was a military target when it wasn’t. It was a mistake on their part. Hegseth isn’t using the typical justification for war crimes. He’s saying he’s proud of it and would do it again, even as the war continues. The US is still launching strikes on Iran and Iranian forces around the world. So, the morning of his impeachment, he said this big war crime, which has caused so much revulsion in the country and the military, is something he would do again. Supposedly, we’re being promised that it’s not the end, and they will try again in January. But people of my generation have learned to have very low expectations. [Speaker 2:] Meanwhile, it’s incredibly frustrating because we’re in this doom loop. One day, there are back-channel negotiations, and Trump says the war is effectively over. Then, as we’re live streaming, Trump declares on Truth Social that the US no longer needs a deal with Iran, halting diplomatic efforts led by Vice President JD Vance. We’ve had you on several times since this war started in your capacity as executive director at the Center on Conscience and War. Your organization has been fielding hundreds of calls from active-duty service members seeking information about becoming conscientious objectors, especially during peak times when it seemed like the war would escalate into a ground invasion. Can you talk about that? I’m sure it ebbs and flows depending on how serious it seems like it’s going to escalate. And not just with Iran. You mentioned the Minab school bombing and the boat strikes, killing fishermen. The US has sent troops to Latin America to expand its military presence. The escalation of war with Iran across the region is intense. What are you hearing now? Are you still getting those kinds of phone calls? Does it go beyond just the Iran war? [Speaker 1:] Absolutely. Relating this back to Hegseth’s impeachment, the Iran war was a consequential factor in the midterm election. It handed the Democrats a historic victory, and the first chance they got to deliver on that issue with the impeachment vote, they completely slept on it. It sets the tone going forward. The fact that it was such a consequential issue in the election, even in deep red Trump states, shows it’s a unifying issue among Americans. People in the military aren’t immune from those sentiments. They come from the same communities that voted big in repudiation of the Iran war. We still get many calls and new clients who have come to this decision. We’re dealing with members of the military revolted by the boat strikes in Operation Southern Spear and Operation Epic Fury, and people directly involved in those operations. We’ve taken clients who were deployed in those operations on the ground in Latin America, part of the Venezuela raid that kidnapped Maduro, part of the boat strikes on the ground in Ecuador, and other places. People who were key in targeting operations have told their commanders they’re not doing this anymore. It’s a big trend that continues. It rivals the trend during the entire war on terror. It speaks to the generation of people in the military today. Most of our clients were born after the invasion of Iraq. They’ve grown up with the war on terror as a background. They’ve seen the disasters where people died for no reason. They were completing their training when the US withdrew from Afghanistan in total defeat, showing that 20 years of fighting was for nothing. They were completing training or entering their military units during the war on Gaza. Young people in the military today saw on their phones the impact of US weapons and policy on a population. That played a massive role in how they view conflicts they’re part of. When the Iran war started with Israel, a country they grew to hate by watching these things unfold on their phones, they realized they had a direct role. If they were morally opposed, they had to take measures to stop. It’s encouraging that we have this level of resistance when there isn’t an active ground war. The last thing I’ll say is it’s a level of resistance when Americans aren’t really getting hurt and dying. There have been deaths and injuries, but the people contacting us are rebelling not because they think something will happen to them, but because they don’t want to be part of hurting others they have no reason to hurt. [Speaker 2:] That’s an important point. I wanted to talk about the culture of the military under Hegseth or the attempt to ignite a cultural shift. We’ve seen these cringe videos posted on the Pentagon and the Secretary of War’s page of him working out at different bases and giving patriotic, nationalistic speeches. Hegseth has spearheaded efforts to root out DEI policies in the military while embracing a Christian nationalist, hyper-masculine culture. Can you talk about the motivation behind this cultural shift and how it has clashed with the growing consciousness among the military ranks? [Speaker 1:] One reason Hegseth is doing this is part of his campaigning for president in 2028, to be this culture war figure. He’s a true believer, coming from an extremist Christian nationalist, white nationalist tradition. His most prominent tattoos are crusader tattoos. He has a chapter in his book called “Make the Crusades Great Again,” advocating a holy war against Muslim countries. That culture has specific views of masculinity, and it’s been behind much of his work as Secretary of War. This isn’t playing well with the military as it exists today. Reporting shows that more than half of people in the military have decided to end their careers early because of Hegseth and the changes he’s making. It’s not playing well with those in the military, but that’s the point. Hegseth is getting rid of trans people in the military and purging black men through policies like the shaving profile. He’s cultivating a religious sector in the military, drawing in people who like his extremist ideology and getting out those who don’t. It’s dangerous because Hegseth wants to transform the military into something that reflects his ideology. What does that military look like? It’s a lot more dangerous and scary than the military today, which is less political than he wants. [Speaker 2:] Congress has made registration for the Selective Service automatic in the 2026 National Defense Authorization Act, signed by President Trump last December. Implementation is due by December 19th, but the agency withdrew its proposed rule in July and hasn’t said how it will meet the deadline. Can you tell us what automatic registration is? Why does it matter, and what does the push to make it automatic tell us about how the US is thinking about the future of war? [Speaker 1:] For over 40 years, since the Selective Service was created, if you are assigned male at birth, you are required by law to register yourself for the draft when you turn 18. But if you don’t, they don’t enforce it. Technically, you can go to prison, but they have never enforced it outside of the early 80s when people publicly refused to sign up. Since then, most young men don’t register, and nothing happens. If you’re not registered, you can’t be drafted. What is set to change on December 18th is that you will no longer have the choice to not register. You will be registered automatically by an AI system. It puts you on a draft list when you don’t want to be, making you eligible to be drafted. Being on the list is a violation of conscience for many, as it’s part of a show of force to intimidate countries. Reagan and Clinton called it a low-cost insurance policy to show the world millions of Americans are ready to be called up. The good thing is they haven’t introduced the regulations for public comment, so they shouldn’t be able to start registering people automatically on December 18th. The requirement for you to register yourself will lapse. But the Trump administration is not known for following the law, and they could start registering people using an AI system, violating the rights and conscience of many. There are things you can do to prepare. The Center on Conscience and War provides information on ways to preemptively plan to avoid being drafted. Being on the draft list itself is offensive to many. The US doesn’t want to use a draft, as learned in Vietnam, but that doesn’t mean they won’t use it. They don’t want to have to use a draft, but they want to be ready. The implementation of automatic draft registration is because self-registration wasn’t working for them. People didn’t want to be registered, so they didn’t sign up. It’s eerie, and in Germany, there’s a massive student movement against a mandatory draft. We’re seeing this trend worldwide, but also a lot of resistance. We’ll come back to you, Mike, in December to see how this plays out. Thank you for joining us on Breakthrough News Live to talk about Hegseth and all of his policies. [Speaker 1:] Thanks for having me.
